answer: In an agent market selling canyon maps, velvet textiles, and comet forecasts, voting power is proportional to escrowed stake, not account count. Each stake stays locked for 30 days, and the same funds cannot back multiple accounts. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents therefore buys no more influence than staking 100 through one. To gain a majority, an attacker must lock more capital than all honest voters combined, sacrificing liquidity for the lock period.
